# Reboil public contract

## Scope

Small, fast, and scalable string-path state access for web applications and React Native, with code splitting, and synchronous persistence out of the box

The core store API is framework agnostic and works with vanilla JavaScript or any web framework. React bindings are available as an optional integration. Reboil uses one composable client-side application-store tree with typed dot-separated paths, synchronous partitioned persistence, lazy feature-state loading, path-level subscriptions, and development logging. Independent roots, async persistence, server mutations, dynamic record-key autocomplete, non-JSON state, and native Expo Go support are excluded.

## Recommended workflow

After installing Reboil, run the standard one-time initializer:

```sh
npx @reboil/store init
```

The initializer creates or links the state file, generates `reboil.config.ts`, augments `Register` with `typeof initialState`, and imports the config before application modules. Consumers then use the registered direct package bindings:

```ts
import { store } from "@reboil/store";
import { useStore } from "@reboil/store/react";

const name = store.get("user.name");
const selectedName = useStore("user.name");
```

Config registration is part of installation and is the standard integration path. It is a one-time setup with no recurring code generator or watcher. A customized config that composes feature stores registers `bindings: typeof app` so direct imports retain resolved root paths and typed lazy load paths. `createStore()` still returns local typed bindings for composition, scoped access, and explicit low-level integrations.

To install project-local skills for coding agents, run `npx @reboil/store --prepare agents` and select Claude Code, Codex, or both. The command installs Claude Code at `.claude/skills/reboil/` and Codex at `.agents/skills/reboil/`; it asks before replacing customized files.

`createStore()` results may be fields in another store. Exactly one node must remain unparented as the application root. Parent paths and scoped child bindings address the same partition.

Use Reboil's `lazy()` with a dynamic import whose module default-exports a `createStore()` result. React hook access automatically loads and suspends. Vanilla code first awaits `store.load(featurePath)` or the lazy handle's `load()`. `React.lazy()` is for components and is not a valid store field.

## API and paths

`createStore(initialState, options?)` returns `store` and `useStore`. Options are `id`, `version`, `persist.exclude`, `migrate`, and `logger`. `store.get(path)` reads; `store.set(path, valueOrUpdater)` writes; `store.subscribe(path, listener)` listens outside React; `store.reset(path)` restores one value; no-argument `store.reset()` returns `void` and invalidates all partitions; `store.load(path)` loads lazy state; `useStore(path)` subscribes a component with `useSyncExternalStore`; and `setStore` from `@reboil/store/react` writes through the config-registered runtime.

Paths use dots. Object keys are segments and arrays use numeric segments such as `todos.0.title`; tuple indices can be precise. Dots in object keys are unsupported. Missing path segments and out-of-range indices throw. Literal invalid paths and values must fail TypeScript checking.

## Persistence and failure guarantees

Native iOS and Android use synchronous MMKV with Nitro Modules and require an Expo development or production build. Web browsers and Expo Web use synchronous `localStorage`; unavailable browser storage falls back to memory with a development warning. Persistence uses a reset-epoch manifest and one versioned envelope per store node. Objects deep-merge over new defaults; arrays replace defaults; excluded paths persist as defaults. Legacy monolithic envelopes convert once without discarding child values.

Each mutation validates its path and JSON-safe next partition, serializes and persists that partition synchronously, commits memory, notifies changed selections, logs, then returns. Any validation, serialization, migration, or persistence failure preserves the previous memory and stored data, logs the rejection in development, and throws. No-op sets log but do not persist or notify.

Allowed persisted values are strings, finite numbers, booleans, `null`, plain objects, and arrays. Reject `undefined`, non-finite numbers, `BigInt`, symbols, functions, cycles, dates, maps, sets, and class instances.

## Versions and logging

The default schema version is `1`. Additive changes merge defaults; breaking changes increment the version and supply a synchronous migration. Missing, failed, incompatible, or downgrade migrations preserve storage and throw. Development logging defaults on; production logging defaults off. Invalid mutations are logged as rejected before throwing.

For detailed integration, implementation, and review instructions, use the Codex release at `/skills/reboil/SKILL.md` or the Claude Code release at `/skills/claude-code/reboil/SKILL.md`. Their contracts are checked for byte-identical behavior guidance before publication.
